choices.text: The virus establishes lifelong latency and reactivates during periods of stress

explanation.summary: There are many norovirus strains, and infection with one does not confer immunity to another, so repeat infections occur throughout life.
explanation.whyCorrect: Norovirus exists as many different strains. Infection with one does not convey immunity to another, so repeated norovirus infections throughout a person's life are possible and expected. This is also why prevention depends on hand washing, avoiding raw or undercooked shellfish, and washing produce rather than on acquired immunity.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Unrelated gastrointestinal illness does not erase immunity to a previously encountered strain.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Norovirus infection is self-limiting and has no specific treatment, so relapse of an untreated case is not the mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Norovirus is an RNA virus and does not integrate into host DNA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Norovirus does not establish latency; each episode is a new infection.

questions.stem: During a norovirus outbreak in a long-term care facility, staff have been using an alcohol-based hand rub between residents, and transmission has continued unabated. Which property of norovirus best explains why this measure is inadequate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The virus forms environmentally resistant endospores on the skin surface

choices.label: B

explanation.summary: Alcohol sanitizers work by disrupting a lipid envelope, which norovirus lacks, making it notoriously resistant to them.
explanation.whyCorrect: Enveloped viruses have a lipid membrane that alcohol-based sanitizers disrupt, inactivating the virus. Norovirus is nonenveloped, so there is no membrane to dissolve and the particle is far more resistant. This is why the CDC recommends hand washing with soap and water, which physically removes virus, rather than alcohol hand rubs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Viruses do not form endospores; that is a bacterial survival structure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Norovirus is shed in stool as well as vomitus and spreads by the fecal-oral route.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Norovirus infects the gastrointestinal tract rather than hiding inside phagocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The 5-minute contact time applies to bleach left on surfaces, not to a universal requirement of all agents.

questions.stem: After a norovirus outbreak in a school cafeteria, the environmental services team asks how to decontaminate the hard surfaces in the kitchen. Which of the following is the recommended approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply a quaternary ammonium cleaner and rinse it off immediately afterward

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply bleach and leave it on the surface for at least 5 minutes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Heat all surfaces and utensils to 145 degrees Fahrenheit for one minute

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use a low-concentration bleach solution and wipe it away at once

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wipe surfaces with 70% isopropyl alcohol and allow them to air dry

explanation.summary: Surface decontamination for norovirus requires bleach left in contact with the surface for at least 5 minutes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Norovirus is highly resistant to many common disinfectants, to heat up to 145 degrees Fahrenheit, and even to low-concentration bleach solutions. The CDC recommendation is therefore to leave bleach on surfaces for at least 5 minutes, along with hand washing using soap and water, cooking shellfish thoroughly, and washing clothes in hot water.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Norovirus resists many common disinfectants, and immediate rinsing eliminates any contact time.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Norovirus is resistant to heat up to 145 degrees Fahrenheit, so this temperature is not reliable.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Norovirus resists low-concentration bleach, and wiping it away at once removes the needed contact time.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Alcohol works on enveloped viruses; nonenveloped norovirus resists it.

questions.stem: Five members of a family become ill after a shared church potluck. Vomiting and watery diarrhea began in all five within a narrow window after the meal, and norovirus is later confirmed. Which of the following best represents the usual incubation period of this virus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1 to 3 hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: 4 to 7 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: 4 to 8 hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: 12 to 23 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: 12 to 48 hours

explanation.summary: Norovirus has a relatively short incubation period averaging 12 to 48 hours.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once infected with norovirus, the incubation period is relatively short, on average 12 to 48 hours. The virus then infects the gastrointestinal tract and produces acute vomiting and watery diarrhea. This short interval is part of why point-source outbreaks appear so explosive.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is far shorter than the norovirus incubation period.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is longer than the usual norovirus incubation period; sapovirus runs 1 to 4 days.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Norovirus symptoms typically begin later than this, on average 12 to 48 hours after exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 12 to 23 days is the incubation period of rubella, not norovirus.
